puzzles.title: Free Lunch!
puzzles.story: The black queen wandered off without a bodyguard. Can your rook grab her?
puzzles.hint: Rooks zoom in straight lines. Look up the a-file!

puzzles.title: The Knight's L-shaped Jump
puzzles.story: Sir Knight spots a lonely bishop. Hop over in one L-shaped jump!
puzzles.hint: Two squares up, one square to the side. Where does that land?

puzzles.title: The Bishop's Secret Slide
puzzles.story: A black rook is hiding in the far corner. Your bishop can slide all the way there!
puzzles.hint: Bishops slide diagonally. Follow the long diagonal from corner to corner.

puzzles.title: Protect the Castle!
puzzles.story: The black king hid behind his pawns, but they've trapped him! Can your rook finish the game?
puzzles.hint: The king cannot move forward. Check him along the back row!

puzzles.title: The Queen's Big Hug
puzzles.story: Your king and queen work as a team. Put the queen right next to the black king, with your king guarding her!
puzzles.hint: Your king protects b7 and a7. Can the queen land on one of them?

puzzles.title: The Rook Wall
puzzles.story: One rook has built a wall on row 7. Bring the other rook to close the door!
puzzles.hint: The black king is stuck on the top row. Attack that whole row!

puzzles.title: Royal Fork
puzzles.story: A knight check that hits two targets at once. Calculate the full sequence.
puzzles.hint: Which knight check also attacks c8?

puzzles.title: Long-Diagonal Skewer
puzzles.story: King and rook are lined up on the same diagonal. Check the king, then collect what is behind it.
puzzles.hint: The a8–h1 diagonal runs through b7 and h1.

puzzles.title: Discovered Check
puzzles.story: Your rook is aimed at the king but your own bishop is in the way. Move it with a threat of its own.
puzzles.hint: Unmask the rook on e1, and put the bishop where it attacks the queen.

puzzles.title: Back-Rank Deflection
puzzles.story: Black's only back-rank defender is the d8 rook. Overload it.
puzzles.hint: Doubled rooks: sacrifice the front one.

puzzles.title: Rook Roller
puzzles.story: Two rooks against a bare king. Cut it off, then deliver mate on the edge.

lessons.title: Setting Up the Board
lessons.blurb: Where every piece lives when the game begins.

steps.text: Every game starts like this. White is at the bottom. Remember: "light on the right!" The bottom-right square is always light.
Queens love their own colour. The white queen starts on a light square, the black queen on a dark one.
Pawns march forward. On their very first move they may jump two squares.

task.prompt: Move the pawn in front of the king two squares forward.

lessons.title: Protect the Castle! (The Rook)
lessons.blurb: The rook zooms in straight lines.

steps.text: The rook looks like a castle tower. It moves in straight lines, up, down, left or right, as far as it wants.

task.prompt: Slide the rook up to the star!

steps.text: A rook captures by landing on an enemy piece in its path.

lessons.title: The Knight's L-shaped Jump
lessons.blurb: The only piece that can jump over others.

steps.text: The knight moves in an L: two squares one way, then one square to the side.

task.prompt: Jump the knight onto the star.

steps.text: Knights can jump right over pieces, even their own pawns!

task.prompt: Jump the b1 knight over the pawns to the star.

lessons.title: Piece Points
lessons.blurb: Which pieces are worth the most?

steps.text: Pawn = 1 point, Knight = 3, Bishop = 3, Rook = 5, Queen = 9. The king is priceless: you can never trade him!
When you can capture two different pieces, pick the one worth more points.

task.prompt: Take the biggest prize with your pawn.

steps.text: When a piece attacks the king, that is CHECK. The king must get out of danger straight away.
CHECKMATE means the king is in check and has no way to escape. That wins the game!

lessons.title: Control the Center
lessons.blurb: e4, d4, e5, d5: the squares that decide openings.

steps.text: The four central squares give pieces maximum scope. A pawn on e4 claims d5 and f5 and opens lines for the queen and bishop.
Develop with tempo: a knight on f3 attacks e5 and supports a later d4.

lessons.title: Forks & Pins
lessons.blurb: Double attacks and pieces that cannot move.

steps.text: A fork attacks two targets at once. Knight forks are the hardest to see because the knight does not move in lines.
An absolute pin: the pinned piece cannot move, because the king is behind it.

task.prompt: Pin the c6 knight to the king.

steps.text: Doubled pawns: two pawns on one file. They cannot protect each other and are easy to block.
Isolated pawn: no friendly pawns on the neighbouring files. Black's d5 pawn controls the center but must be defended by pieces.
Passed pawn: no enemy pawn can stop it. "Passed pawns must be pushed."
Black answers 1.e4 with 1...c5, fighting for d4 from the side instead of mirroring White.
White develops and prepares d4.
3.d4 opens the center. Black trades the c-pawn for the d-pawn: a half-open c-file for Black, a development lead for White.
Recapture with the knight: this is the Open Sicilian.

lessons.title: Rook Endgames: Building a Bridge
lessons.blurb: The Lucena position, the most important rook ending.

steps.text: White wants to promote on b8 but the king is in the way. First, cut the black king off with a check on the d-file.
Now the key idea: rook to the 4th rank. When the king steps out and the black rook checks from the side, your rook blocks on the 4th. That is the "bridge".
